title: New evidence alters plan for inquest into three custody deaths
subtitle: New evidence has delayed a coroner's inquest into the 2019 death of a woman held in London police custody.
article: "New evidence has come to light and it is in the best interest of the inquest to have the Amanda Bolt inquest proceed at a later date," a spokesperson for the Office of the Chief Coroner of Ontario told The London Free Press.
Bolt, 28, died Nov. 13, 2019, in hospital after she was found unresponsive in a London police cell 10 days earlier.
An inquest into her death and two others who had been in London police custody was to begin Monday, Feb. 17. Instead, an inquest only into the two other deaths is set to start Friday.

"Upon reviewing everything for the inquest, there were some details that may have been overlooked regarding her care. So, they're doing some reviewing and assessing," her brother Chris Bolt said. "There were some new details that came to light so there needs to be some further investigation into that."

Amanda Bolt was arrested the morning Nov. 2, 2019, taken to police headquarters and released, according to Ontario's Special Investigations Unit (SIU). The SIU investigates police actions involving serious injury or death.
Later that day, Bolt was re-arrested for breaching conditions of her release, and was taken back to the police station and put in a cell, the SIU determined.
The next morning, Bolt "went into medical distress" and was taken to hospital and placed on life support, the SIU said. She died in hospital Nov. 13.

Bolt had told the officer in charge of the police detention unit she need medications for a heart condition and other conditions, and asked to be taken to hospital to get those medications, according to an internal police report presented to the London police services board in 2022.
The officer arranged instead to get the medication from a pharmacy the next day, according to the report.
After the investigation by the SIU, London police Sgt. Kevin Lui was charged with failing to provide the necessaries of life.
Those charges were withdrawn Oct. 18, 2021.

"Medical opinions submitted by the Crown and defence both concurred with the pathologist who conducted the deceased's post-mortem and reviewed her medical history, that the lack of heart medication did not cause or contribute to her death," the internal London police report said.
Neither the chief coroner's office nor Chris Bolt would say what new evidence surfaced to lead to the delay of the inquest.
"Every day we still think about her. It's never not hurting," Bolt said.
Coroner's inquests are charged with determining cause of death and juries may make recommendations to prevent similar deaths.

"The thought she will be able to help other people not end up in the same situation is comforting," Bolt said. "From what I've seen, the police department could use some changes when it comes to the people they have detained there."
The inquest into the deaths of Fabian Hart, 46, and Christopher Campbell, 55, is set to begin Friday and last two weeks.
Hart was arrested Feb. 1, 2021, for allegedly failing to comply with release conditions and taken to the police station.
The next day, he told officers he wasn't feeling well and was taken to hospital after going into "medical distress," the SIU said. Hart died Feb. 2, 2021.
Campbell was arrested on Oct. 11, 2018, after police responded to a report of a motorist driving erratically.
He became unresponsive while being driven to the police station, and was taken to hospital where he died.
The SIU cleared officers involved in the custody of Hart and Campbell of any wrongdoing.
